Green Bay entered this contest sitting last place in the NFC North with a 5-3 record. In one of the toughest divisions in football, Jordan Love and his team needed to do everything they could to stay in the divisional race. The Packers did that and then some on Sunday evening . Green Bay dominated the Patriots on the road. The Packers came away with a monster 45-27 victory thanks to a three-touchdown performance against New England’s defense. It’s a big win, but Love is already hyper- focused on the mission ahead of his team. “The mindset has to be complete focus and preparation on Minnesota,” said Love, via Zach Jacobson of PackerDispatch.com. “You can’t let one game lull you to sleep; it’s a great performance tonight, but it’s about getting back to work.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Love was on his game on Sunday evening as well. He threw for 372 yards while tossing three touchdowns in this game. Two wide receivers — Matthew Golden and Christian Watson — made up the bulk of their receiving yards. Both pass catchers racked up more than 160 yards receiving. Green Bay’s defense was also up to the task. They sacked Patriots quarterback Drake Maye four times in this game. They also picked him off three times. Xavier McKinney had two of them, marking his second two-interception game of the season. The Packers are looking to win the NFC North once again. Performances like this will certainly help. They will need to bring this fire to their clash next week with the division-leading Minnesota Vikings in Week 10. item.title: 49ers star Christian McCaffrey sets new RB record after passing Marshall Faulk in Raiders game
item.description: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images 49ers star Christian McCaffrey sets new RB record after passing Marshall Faulk in Raiders game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey once again stole the show, reaching another career milestone during Sunday’s 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. With his 37th career receiving touchdown, McCaffrey moved past Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk for the most receiving scores by a running back in the Super Bowl era. The 30-year-old entered the 2026 season tied with Faulk at 36 touchdown receptions. However, he claimed sole possession of the record with a 12-yard touchdown catch from quarterback Brock Purdy with 5:15 remaining in the second quarter. The score extended San Francisco’s lead to 21-7 and was his second touchdown of the afternoon. McCaffrey had already opened his scoring account with a 1-yard rushing score to finish off the 49ers’ first offensive possession. He finished the contest with 18 carries for 68 yards and two touchdowns, adding two receptions for 19 yards. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) McCaffrey’s latest accomplishment also ended a nine-game stretch without a receiving touchdown. His previous scoring drought was the longest of his career, although he caught two touchdown passes in last season’s wild-card round. Now having reached 37 career receiving touchdowns, McCaffrey is tied for fifth place on the NFL’s all-time list among running backs, alongside Johnny “Blood” McNally. Hall of Famer Lenny Moore remains at the top with 48 receiving touchdowns. Moore played as a flanker and halfback between 1956 and 1967. The record-setting performance came after McCaffrey dealt with a mild hamstring strain during the Niners’ Week 7 loss to the Atlanta Falcons. The Week 8 bye provided additional recovery time, allowing him to handle 20 touches against Las Vegas without any reported signs of lingering physical problems. McCaffrey’s latest accomplishment follows an impressive 2025 campaign in which he accumulated 2,126 scrimmage yards and 17 scrimmage touchdowns, tying his career high with his touchdown receptions. San Francisco, meanwhile, improved to 7-1, maintaining its position atop the NFC standings. The 49ers will now turn their attention to a Week 10 road matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, with McCaffrey looking to stretch his seven-game touchdown streak. item.title: Rutgers football listed as a 13.5-point underdog against Nebraska
item.description: LINCOLN, NEBRASKA - OCTOBER 5: Isaac Gifford #2 of the Nebraska Cornhuskers and Marques Buford Jr. #3 team up to stop Ian Strong #9 of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights during the third quarter at Memorial Stadium on October 5, 2024 in Lincoln, Nebraska. (Photo by Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) | Getty Images After getting thrashed by Wisconsin 31-10 last weekend, Rutgers football is listed as a near two-touchdown underdog this weekend at home against Nebraska. To be more specific, FanDuel has the Scarlet Knights listed as 13.5-point underdogs with the over/under being listed at 53.5 points. Rutgers will be searching for its first win ever over the Cornhuskers in this game, as Nebraska is currently a perfect 7-0 against the Knights. Rutgers will be coming into this game on a three-game losing streak, falling to Northwestern and Wisconsin in blowout fashion and being defeated by a struggling Michigan team. Similar to the Knights, the Cornhuskers are on a long losing streak of their own, falling to Indiana, Oregon, Washington and Illinois in consecutive weeks. However, unlike Rutgers, three of these losses came by a touchdown or less. Anthony Colandrea, the Cornhuskers’ starting quarterback, has had a decent season so far, throwing for 2,100 yards and 16 touchdowns. However, his play has taken a serious step down in this losing streak for the Huskers, as over the last four games he has thrown three touchdowns and five interceptions. His passing yards haven’t decreased much over this stretch, but those yards have not translated into touchdowns. His best receiving option so far this season has been Kwazi Gilmer, who has 46 catches for 603 yards and seven touchdowns so far this season. Colandrea is also a decent runner, rushing for an average of 4.5 yards per carry as well as four total touchdowns this season. This is a concern for Rutgers, which has historically struggled against mobile quarterbacks. Nebraska has two solid options in their running back room, Jamal Rule and Mekhi Nelson. So far this season, Rule has carried the ball 88 times for 632 yards and five touchdowns, while Nelson has 78 carries for 348 yards and five touchdowns. Having these two increases the likelihood of Nebraska wearing down the Knights’ poor rush defense. Defensively, Nebraska is led in tackles by linebacker Owen Chambliss, while lineman Jahsear Whittington leads the Cornhuskers’ pass rush with 4.5 sacks. In most years, this game could be seen as the perfect opportunity for the Knights to get their first-ever win against the free-falling Huskers. However, since Rutgers is also in a free fall and might be without several of its top offensive talents again, it is hard to see Nebraska not using this game to “get right.” The score differential will likely depend heavily on who is actually available for Rutgers. Rutgers vs. Nebraska will take place at home on Saturday, November 14, at 12:30 p.m. The game will be broadcast live on the Big Ten Network.

Guiliano Simeone put the hosts ahead after just 10 minutes but Barcelona hit back through a Fermin Lopez double to seal an important win. Cubarsi revealed afterwards how Barca made changes at the break that helped to swing the match in their favor. “In the first half we came out a bit disconnected. They had a great first half, but at half-time we were able to fix the things we weren’t doing well and we took the victory,” he said. “We needed to apply better high pressure, and in the second half we positioned ourselves a bit better. item.title: Austin Reaves celebrates the Lakers being able to win big games without Luka Doncic
item.description: Austin Reaves celebrates the Lakers being able to win big games without Luka Doncic originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In nine games played this season, Luka Doncic has been spectacular for the Los Angeles Lakers . He is averaging a whopping 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 7.7 assists per game. He has been the primary reason behind the Lakers ' impressive success at the start of the season. Doncic had to sit out the Lakers' Sunday night game against the Detroit Pistons because of back tightness. That is a worrying sign for the Lakers because back injuries are tough to navigate. However, it seems the Lakers managed to push through without their superstar leading the charge. Austin Reaves lauds how the Lakers won a big game without Luka Doncic After losing LeBron James in the summer, the Lakers have pivoted to fully focusing on maximizing Doncic. That has paid off so far, but there are times when he has to sit out games due to a nagging injury he has been dealing with. Sunday was the best example of this because Doncic is currently dealing with back tightness. Thankfully for the Lakers and their fans, they have Austin Reaves leading the charge. He played like Doncic on Sunday, scoring 43 points to lead the Lakers over the Pistons . MORE: Luka Doncic speaks on what he has improved in his game after joining the Lakers It was an impressive performance from the Lakers because the Pistons are one of the best teams in the Eastern Conference. Moving forward, this is a good sign for the Lakers because they have found a way to keep winning without their best player leading the way. "We just stayed calm; you can get sped up in those moments, but we trust what we got on this team. You got to weather the storm, and that's what we did... We got a lot of guys who can play basketball; they play the right way, they play hard, they know their roles, unselfish guys who are ready to step up when their name is called," Reaves said in his post-game interview after beating the Pistons . The Lakers are humming positively this season, and that bodes well for the long season. Of course, it is still early, so they are building the right habits that can help them thrive during the Playoffs in April. At the moment, they are enjoying the process and aiming to keep developing. Hellebuyck returns to Winnipeg as a member of the Devils on Tuesday, and he is expected to face the noise from Jets fans after he demanded a trade and sat out the start of the season until getting his wish with the deal that sent him to New Jersey. "This has been an organizational decision for us that we've debated at length," Devils GM Sunny Mehta said in a statement Sunday. item.title: ‘I’m Ready’ – Magomed Magomedov Eyes Lightweight MMA Gold After Hard-Fought Win At ONE Fight Night 49
item.description: Undefeated Bahraini standout Magomed Magomedov turned in a night to remember in his ONE Championship debut, and the Dagestani-trained athlete could not be more pleased with how his maiden outing in the world’s largest martial arts organization played out. The 31-year-old improved to a spotless 16-0 with a tough split-decision triumph over Brazilian star Lucas Gabriel in their lightweight MMA clash at ONE Fight Night 49 on Prime Video inside Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium, which broadcast live on Friday, November 6. Photo Credit: ONE Championship Stepping onto the global stage in front of millions of fans around the world is a moment most athletes only dream about. But Magomedov did it in the main event of a stacked U.S. primetime card with an unbeaten record to protect. He looked back on a memorable night with plenty to say. Magomedov told onefc.com: “I’m very happy that I got a chance to get a debut in ONE Championship. I was so happy that I got a debut with a very, very good fighter as well. He was very strong. He was on a series of wins. But I knew myself, I knew I could fight him, and I could win.” View this post on Instagram Gabriel undoubtedly lived up to that high praise, but Magomedov’s suffocating pressure dictated the early tempo. He quickly turned the battle into a complex grappling puzzle, dragging his foe to the canvas and grinding away from top position through most of the opening frame. He continued hunting the takedown in round two, even as Gabriel frantically fought his way out of the grappling exchanges. Round three featured a late surge from the Brazilian, who successfully reversed a scramble and landed heavy knees from top control. However, the late rally was not quite enough to sway the overall scorecards, as two of the three judges rightfully sided with the unbeaten newcomer. Magomedov left the ring with his hand raised , though the split verdict gave him firm opinions on the scoring criteria. He said: “I had more positive moments than my opponent. I’m not very sure why I got the split decision, because I feel like the first two rounds were mine, and then maybe he got the last round only. “[But] generally speaking, I think I got the win because of my pressure and dominance. item.title: Justin Herbert weapon offers eye-popping take on Chargers’ epic failure
item.description: The Los Angeles Chargers fell to 0-8 for the season on Sunday, losing to the Houston Texans, 44-22. The defense had arguably its worst game of the season. But, the Chargers offense finally scored a touchdown for the first time since Week 5. In their eighth straight loss of the season, the Chargers snapped a streak that lasted 37 consecutive drives (11 quarters of football) until Quentin Johnston’s score against the Texans. Reporters asked tight end Charlie Kolar about the nightmare streak, which he didn’t know about. Will Anderson Jr. #51 of the Houston Texans greets Charlie Kolar #88 of the Los Angeles Chargers after the game at SoFi Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Inglewood, California. Getty Images “37!?” Kolar said. “I wish you never told me that.” Kolar, who joined the Chargers on a three-year, $24.3 million deal in the offseason, might have just delivered the most honest answer about the team’s 2026 season. “We’re 0-8. It is so hard to mentally and emotionally be present. I didn’t even know that we hadn’t scored (a touchdown) in that long,” Kolar said. Charlie Kolar #88 of the Los Angeles Chargers runs against Jake Hansen #35 of the Houston Texans during the first half at SoFi Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Inglewood, California. Getty Images “What was the question? I’m sorry.” The Chargers have been reluctant to admit the campaign is a losing season, but with an 0-8 record, the team looks impractical acting like nothing has to change. And yet, the front office is reportedly unwilling to trade any of its players ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline . The Chargers are at rock bottom, but their refusal to understand where they are has hindered any progress for the team this year. Kolar’s answer is perhaps the most authentic response to the Chargers’ winless season. item.title: Flyers Postgame Blog: 3 Blown Leads & a Stolen Point
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was another disappointing loss for the Philadelphia Flyers on Sunday, who fell 4-3 in overtime to the Calgary Flames. The Flyers were getting pressed early on, but flipped a switch halfway through the first period. They looked like an unstoppable team that was sticking to and executing a game plan. The Flyers grabbed the lead in the first period, but lost it when the Flames tied it before the intermission. Then, right out of the first intermission, Philly took the lead early in the second period, just to concede it minutes later. A big power-play goal regained the lead for the Flyers before the second break, giving them the lead entering the third period. The Flames amped up the effort and were really doing everything they could to break even. Philly blew the lead while on the power play, giving up a shorthanded goal to blow their third lead. Following the shorty, the Flames were dialed in and had too many high-danger chances to count, but Dan Vladar played out of his mind to keep the Flyers in the game. Then, overtime mistakes cost the Flyers the game once again. It was another game where the Flyers put forward a really solid effort in the first two periods, and ruined it in the third period. Read More: Flyers Blow Another 3rd Period Lead, Fall 4-3 vs. Flames Dan Vladar Stole a Point for the Flyers Dan Vladar was incredible for the Flyers on Sunday. He finished the game with 22 saves on 26 shots, but his night was so much better than that. Dan Vladar quite literally stole a point for the Flyers with his efforts late in the game. After the Flames had tied the game up, they had countless chances to take the lead before regulation was over. More than half of the chances they had should have been scored, but they weren’t. Vladar put the Flyers on his back and kept those pucks out of the net, forcing the game to overtime and stealing a point for the Flyers. It was a point that the Flyers don’t deserve, either. If it weren’t for Vladar, that point is not there. Vladar stood tall when it mattered most, but once again, his team could not get him the win. Owen Tippett Looked More Like Himself If there were any positives to take from the game, it’s that Owen Tippett is starting to look like himself again. item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 08: Roko Prkacin #8 of the Penn State Nittany Lions drives to the basket int he second half during a college basketball game against the Pittsburgh Panthers at The Palestra on November 8, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Penn State kept it close with Pitt for most of the game on Sunday, but the Lions came up short in an 82-76 loss at the Palestra. The offense committed 16 turnovers and struggled to shoot from the floor in the second half. It was certainly a more competitive showing than last year’s drubbing in Hershey, but it was not enough for Penn State to pull out a win. The first half was tight and had very little flow for long stretches of the game, as both teams racked up a high number of fouls early in the half. Penn State finally got some separation when Brant Byers hit back-to-back threes with just over five minutes left in the half. The Nittany Lions led 35-28 and had momentum, but just as quickly as they built a lead, the Panthers closed out the half on a 14-3 run. Penn State had three turnovers that led to easy transition baskets for Pitt and turned the momentum of the game on its head. Pitt took a 42-38 lead to the locker room. The hot shooting from both teams cooled off in the second half, and although Pitt led throughout, Penn State hung around. A’lahn Sumler set the tone with a pair of threes in the first few minutes of the second half that helped Pitt open up a seven-point lead, but the Panthers could not stretch the lead any further. Penn State made just nine field goals in the second half and needed to rely on its advantage at the free throw line to make up the difference. Penn State continued to trail by a modest margin, but poor interior defense left Baye Ndongo open for a dunk with under two minutes left that extended Pitt’s lead to 77-69. Penn State did not go quietly, as a three from Ivan Juric and a quick steal and layup by Josh Reed cut the deficit to 77-74, but Pitt held off the late charge with three free throws and a forced turnover on Penn State’s final possession. The Panthers came away with an 82-76 win at the Palestra. item.title: Lakers star Austin Reaves perfectly sums up LA’s win vs. Pistons without Luka Doncic
item.description: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images Lakers star Austin Reaves perfectly sums up LA’s win vs. Pistons without Luka Doncic appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Austin Reaves carried the Los Angeles Lakers on Sunday, and he made it clear the team never panicked when things got tight against the Detroit Pistons. With Luka Doncic sidelined due to low back tightness, Reaves erupted for a season-high 43 points as the Lakers held off the Pistons 121-116 at Little Caesars Arena. Afterward, he summed up the win in simple terms. “We just stayed calm. You can get sped up in those types of moments, but we trust what we got on this team. You just got to weather the storm sometimes, and that’s what we did. We played a good fourth quarter and got a really big win against a really good team,” Reaves said after the game . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “You just got to weather the storm sometimes.” Austin Reaves joins @roquitheus after his season-high 43-point night to talk about the #Lakers ’ fourth-quarter response, trust in their depth and stepping up without Luka. 💪 pic.twitter.com/sAJKiDMlRC — Spectrum SportsNet (@SpectrumSN) November 9, 2026 The Lakers had a storm to weather. Los Angeles raced out to a 38-14 lead after the first quarter and led by as many as 26 points. Detroit fought back, cutting the deficit to three in the third quarter behind a hot-shooting bench. The Pistons never led, however, and Reaves and company did just enough down the stretch to close it out. Reaves was nearly flawless. He knocked down 14 of his 27 shots, went 4-of-6 from beyond the arc and a perfect 11-of-11 from the free-throw line. He added five rebounds and four assists while committing just one turnover. He also credited the Lakers’ depth, which was on full display . Walker Kessler posted 12 points and 16 rebounds, while Collin Sexton and Ziaire Williams each chipped in 17 points. “We got a lot of guys that can play basketball. They play the right way, they play hard, they know their roles, and unselfish guys that are ready to step up when their name’s called,” Reaves said. Still, Reaves knows the Lakers will need that same mindset once Doncic returns. “Obviously, when we get Luka back, everybody’s got to have the same mentality. He’s one of the best players in the league, if not the best player in the league, and we got to do what we got to do to help him be successful and our organization be successful,” he said. For Detroit, Daniss Jenkins exploded for 31 points on eight 3-pointers, while Kevin Huerter added 24. The Lakers improved to 10-2 and will wrap up their back-to-back against the Atlanta Hawks on Monday. item.title: Andy Reid Fires Back at Media Over Failed QB Sneak vs. Jets
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 25: Head coach Andy Reid of the Kansas City Chiefs looks on against the Seattle Seahawks during the first quarter at Lumen Field on October 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs ended up having a nice day offensively during their 35-12 win over the New York Jets. However, things started off a bit rocky for the unit. On two of its first three possessions, Kansas City lost a fumble and punted. The former occurred while backup quarterback Justin Fields attempted to execute a quarterback sneak during a third-and-one situation. Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid Fires Back at Media Over Failed QB Sneak Reid was grilled several times by the media this past week for not running a QB sneak during a third-and-goal situation against the Denver Broncos. It is a controversial topic because Reid has refused to run the play ever since Patrick Mahomes was injured while performing one back in 2019. Perhaps out of spite, Reid called a QB sneak on the Chiefs’ opening possession of the game with Fields. Not only did Fields not get the yard necessary for a first down, but he fumbled the snap and the Jets recovered it. Reid gave a snarky response to the media when asked why he finally decided to call a QB sneak. “You guys asked for it, so we gave it to you, and it didn’t work, how’d you feel?” Reid said. “Those are hard to practice. Quarterback sneaks are hard to practice unless you do it in a game. We just got to get those two (Fields, center Creed Humphrey) on the same page on it, make sure we get the ball up first in the quarterback’s hands.” Chiefs Scored Season High Amount of Points vs. Jets 35 points is the most Kansas City has scored in a game so far this season. Running back Kenneth Walker III looked like his usual self after a couple of down outings. He took 18 carries for 102 yards and one rushing touchdown. Walker also added four receptions for 41 yards and two receiving touchdowns. Mahomes had a stellar day as well, throwing for 242 yards on 23 completions and two touchdowns. Despite sustaining what appeared to be a painful injury to his elbow , Mahomes continued to play and perform well, hitting seven different receivers on the day. The Chiefs racked up 391 total yards of offense against the Jets. Backup running back Emmett Johnson continued to prove he can make plays in relief of Walker, as he averaged 5.7 yards per carry and scored a touchdown. Tight end Travis Kelce led all pass catchers in receiving yards with 72. item.title: Giants WR Malik Nabers Issues Fiery Response to ‘Body Language’ Criticism
item.description: New York Giants WR Malik Nabers. Getty When does a win not quite feel like a win? For New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers, probably following Sunday’s 19-11 win over the Philadelphia Eagles — a game in which Nabers came off the field to questions about his body language and being a bad teammate after he saw his 4-game streak of 100-yard receiving games snapped with 5 receptions for 48 yards. Nabers was visibly frustrated during the game, including slamming his helmet on the sideline and throwing one hand up in frustration after quarterback J.J. McCarthy missed a throw into a tight window late in the game. Nabers closed out his day by dropping a perfect pass from McCarthy in the end zone that would have made it a two-score game in the fourth quarter. After Fox Sports play-by-play man Joe Davis and color commentator and former NFL tight end Greg Olsen were highly critical of Nabers during the broadcast, Nabers fired back on social media after the game. “Y’all be trying to create a narrative on me so bad it’s actually crazy!!!” Nabers wrote on his official Instagram account on Sunday . “If you don’t like the way I play the game keep the camera off me!! SIMPLE! But (Greg Olsen) callin’ me a bad teammate when every team I’ve been on, NOBODY I’ve played with has said (that) about me is crazy! My face is the same way if I’m having a good game, bad, winning or losing. If it’s a problem: 1. Keep the camera off me, 2. Pray about it! Simple.” What Davis and Olsen Said About Nabers Davis and Olsen went in on Nabers after McCarthy missed on an attempt to Nabers in the second half. “His body language has been terrible today,” Davis said. “It’s not good,” Fox Sports color commentator and former NFL tight end Greg Olsen said. “There’s a fine line between being demanding and chasing greatness and then being a bad teammate … like if your teammate scores a touchdown for the lead and you’re still worried about your touches.” Nabers did nothing to help his cause by dropping a perfect pass from McCarthy in the end zone that would have given the Giants a 20-8 lead in the fourth quarter. Instead, the Giants settled for a field goal and a 16-8 lead. “You can’t act like that and drop that pass,” Olsen said. “That’s a perfectly thrown ball.” The Giants improved to 5-2-1 and are still alone in first place in the NFC East. The Packers safety went on to return the interception all the way to the New England 9-yard line.
